scope: Existing packaged file inventory; playback and human listening are separate gates.

rows.text: Make a choice, then explain what you found.
Learn by exploring, sorting and spotting useful clues.
Learn first, then try it independently.
A prediction is an idea, not a wrong answer.
Prediction saved. Now compare it with the observation. A prediction is an idea, not a wrong answer.
Not quite. Which clue is older? Try again.
A country is a place inside a continent. Look at the map positions and try again.
Good detective work. Look closely and try another answer.
A continent is a large area of land. An ocean is a huge area of salt water. A country is a place where people live. A map helps us find places.
The past is what happened before now. Evidence is a clue that helps us learn. A sequence puts events in order.
Scientists observe, sort and classify. Plants and animals are living things; materials are what objects are made from; seasons bring different weather.
Africa is between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans. Kenya and Egypt are in Africa.
Asia is the largest continent. Japan and India are in Asia.
Europe is north of Africa. The United Kingdom and France are in Europe.
Find North America on the map.
Canada and Mexico are in North America.
Find South America on the map.
Brazil and Peru are in South America.
Australia is the continent. Oceania is a wider region that includes Australia, New Zealand and Pacific islands.
Antarctica is the cold continent at the bottom of the map. It has no countries.
Which map key would help a sailor find the harbour?
A map key explains symbols. An anchor can show a harbour.
A map key explains symbols. Look for the symbol that sailors use.
Which way is east on our map?
With north at the top, east is to the right.
Check the north arrow: east is to the right when north is at the top.
The Pacific Ocean is the biggest ocean.
Which ocean is around the North Pole?
The Arctic Ocean is around the North Pole.
Which is a physical feature of a place?
A beach is a natural physical feature. A school and road are human-made features.
Physical features are natural. A beach is made by nature; buildings and roads are human-made.
Guide the boat to the treasure using compass directions.
You followed north, east, north, east. A compass and map help us describe a route.
That way reaches water or leaves the map. Use the north arrow and follow the clear squares.
What is the capital city of England?
London is the capital city of England and of the United Kingdom.
England is one of the four UK countries. Its capital city is London.
What is the capital city of Wales?
Cardiff is the capital city of Wales.
Wales is one of the four UK countries. Its capital city is Cardiff.
What is the capital city of Scotland?
Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.
Scotland is one of the four UK countries. Its capital city is Edinburgh.
What is the capital city of Northern Ireland?
Belfast is the capital city of Northern Ireland.
Northern Ireland is one of the four UK countries. Its capital city is Belfast.
Which sea or ocean is west of the United Kingdom?
The Atlantic Ocean is west of the United Kingdom.
Use the compass: west is left on a north-up map. The Atlantic Ocean is west of the UK.
Which sea is east of Great Britain?
The North Sea is east of Great Britain.
The North Sea is on the east side of Great Britain.
Which sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland?
The Irish Sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland.
Look for the sea between the two land areas: it is the Irish Sea.
Which waterway is south of England?
The English Channel is south of England.
The English Channel is the waterway south of England.
Which ocean is between the Americas and Europe/Africa?
The Atlantic Ocean sits between these continents.
Which ocean is between Africa, Asia and Australia?
The Indian Ocean is between Africa, Asia and Australia.
Which tool is shaped more like the round Earth?
A globe is a round model of Earth. A flat map spreads places onto a page or screen.
Earth is round, so a globe is the round model. A map is usually flat.
Why might an explorer use a flat map?
A flat map can show places on a page, although it cannot show a round Earth perfectly.
Maps show places. A flat map is easy to spread out and label.
It can spread out on a page
What does an aerial photograph show?
An aerial photograph is a photograph taken from above a place. It shows real details at that time.
Aerial means from the air or above. Choose the answer about a real place viewed from above.
Which picture is a plan view?
A plan is a simple drawing or map seen from above. It can use symbols and a key.
A plan view is a simple drawing from above, often with symbols.
What can a digital map on a tablet help you do?
A digital map can be explored on a screen. Many digital maps let people zoom and search.
Digital maps are maps on screens. Think about actions such as zooming and searching.
A rain shower observed today is an example of…
Weather describes what the air is like now or over a short time, such as today’s rain.
A single day or shower tells us about weather. Climate describes usual patterns over many years.
Climate is the usual pattern of weather in a place over a long time.
Climate is about usual weather patterns over many years, not one moment.
Which statement is a careful comparison?
Some tropical places are often warm, but weather can change. We should not say every island is the same.
Geographers make careful comparisons. Places can have patterns, but daily weather can change.
A tropical island is often warm, but its weather can still change.
Every island has the same weather every day.
We record one cool, rainy day near our school. What can we say?
One observation tells us about that place and time. More observations are needed to describe a climate pattern.
Keep the claim close to the evidence: one observation tells us about that day, not every day.
That day’s weather was cool and rainy.
We know the whole climate now.
Japan is an island country in Asia.
Brazil is a country in South America.
Kenya is a country in Africa.
Australia is the continent. Oceania is a wider region around it.
A time detective wants to learn what an old seaside holiday looked like. Which clue is most useful?
An old photograph can show visible details, but it cannot tell us everything people thought or felt.
Choose a clue made at the time. A source can help, but every source has limits.
Which source could help us investigate a castle long ago?
An artefact is one object from the past. Historians compare it with other sources.
Look for something connected to the castle in the past. Historians compare more than one clue.
A map of a future city
Put these ways to send a message from oldest to newest.
A handwritten letter is older than a landline telephone, which is older than a smartphone message.
Put these lights from oldest to newest.
People used fire before candles, and electric lightbulbs came later.
A photograph of an old house can show us what?
A photograph is useful evidence for what a place looked like, but it cannot show every thought.
Sources have limits: a photograph can show what we see, not someone’s thoughts.
Which clues could help us find out how a local school changed?
Photographs and an interview give different clues. Memories and pictures can both leave things out.
Local historians compare clues connected to the place, such as photographs and people’s memories.
Put these parts of a person’s story from earliest to latest.
A personal timeline starts with being a baby, then a child, then an adult. People grow at different rates.
Put these school photographs in time order using their dates.
Dates help us order sources. 1990 came before 2010, and 2010 came before 2025.
A former pupil remembers the playground. What can their interview tell us?
An interview can share one person’s memory. Historians compare it with photographs and other clues before making a wider claim.
One interview tells us about that person’s memory, not everyone’s experience.
An old photo shows a small playground. A former pupil remembers a larger one. What should a time detective do?
Sources can show different details. Check dates, ask another question and compare another photograph or plan.
When clues differ, compare more evidence and check when each source was made.
An old photograph shows a shop front. Which conclusion is safest?
A photograph is useful for visible details, but it does not tell us everything about people or events.
A photograph can show visible details. It cannot show every thought or tell the whole story.
We can describe how it looked.
We know everything about the shop.
Which pair gives two different kinds of clues about how a local street changed?
An old photo can show what the street looked like, while a modern map can show today’s layout. Comparing them helps us notice change.
Choose sources connected to the street and made at different times.
An old photo and a modern map
Put these communication clues from oldest to newest.
A handwritten letter came before typewriters, landline telephones and smartphone messages.
An oak tree is a plant. It grows and needs light and water.
A plant grows. A fox is an animal and a rock is not living.
A frog is an animal. Animals move, feed and grow.
A fern is a plant and glass is a material. A frog is the animal.
A window must be see-through. Which material is useful?
Clear glass is transparent, so we can see through it. The window is the object; glass is its material.
Think about the property the object needs. A window needs a transparent material.
Which season often has the warmest days?
Summer often has the warmest days, although weather can change.
Winter is usually colder. Summer often has the warmest days.
A rabbit is a mammal. Trout are fish and frogs are amphibians.
A rabbit is a mammal. Look at the group names: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.
A robin is a bird. A lizard is a reptile and a cat is a mammal.
What does a green plant need to grow?
Plants need water and light to grow.
Plants need water and light, not a television or a sandwich.
Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
Roots take in water from the soil and help hold the plant in place.
Look below the soil: roots take in water and hold the plant.
A scientist wants to see how a plant changes. What should they do?
Scientists observe closely and record changes over time.
A fair investigation needs careful observations and records, not one guess.
Predict: two similar seedlings get the same light and warmth. Only one gets water. What might happen?
Your prediction came first. Then you compared it with the observation. This test gives evidence that growing seedlings need water.
After seven days, the watered seedling is green and taller. The seedling without water has wilted.
Use what was observed: the watered seedling grew better in this test.
A cow is a herbivore because it eats plants. A lion is a carnivore and a fox can eat both plants and animals.
Herbivores eat plants. A cow is the herbivore here.
Which word describes an animal that eats plants and other animals?
An omnivore eats plants and other animals.
An omnivore eats both plants and other animals.
Which body part is linked with seeing?
We use our eyes to see. Ears help with hearing and the nose helps with smelling.
Eyes are linked with seeing. Ears help us hear and noses help us smell.
Which one is a common flowering plant?
A daisy is a common flowering plant. A rabbit is an animal and a brick is a material.
A flowering plant has flowers. A daisy is the plant.
Which tree usually keeps its leaves through winter?
Evergreen trees usually keep leaves throughout the year. Deciduous trees lose their leaves at a season each year.
Evergreen means the tree usually keeps its leaves. Deciduous trees lose leaves each year.
Which part helps hold a plant upright and carries water upwards?
The stem helps support the plant and carries water to other parts.
The stem supports the plant and carries water. Petals and seeds have different jobs.
In “a wooden chair”, which word names the material?
A chair is an object. Wood is the material it can be made from.
The object is the chair. The material is wood.
Which material is usually useful for keeping rain out of a raincoat?
Plastic can be waterproof, so it can help keep rain out. The exact material and design still matter.
A raincoat needs a material that keeps water out. Plastic can be waterproof.
Which material is usually absorbent for wiping up a small spill?
Paper can absorb water. Glass and metal are usually not absorbent.
Absorbent materials soak up liquid. Paper is the best choice here.
Which record could help us compare weather each day?
A dated weather chart lets us compare observations across days.
To compare weather, record observations with dates in a chart or table.
Which change might we observe as spring begins?
Plants may grow new leaves or flowers in spring. Weather varies, so this is an observation to check, not a promise for every day.
Buds opening can be a spring change. Keep seasonal statements as observations, because weather varies.
Which is a question a scientist could investigate?
A simple question can be tested by observing and recording what happens.
Choose a question that can be explored with an observation or simple test.
What is the best thing ever?
To compare two paper towels fairly, what should we try to keep the same?
Keeping the amount of water the same makes the comparison fairer. We can change one thing and observe the result.
Keep important conditions the same so the comparison is fair.
Which tool can help us observe a small leaf closely?
A hand lens magnifies small details so we can observe closely.
A hand lens helps us see small details.
Which way could we record how many red and green leaves we found?
A tally table helps us count and compare groups of observations.
Use a table or tally to record and compare observations.
Predict: which object will make the longest shadow near a lamp, a small bead or a tall block?
We made a prediction, observed the test and used the result to answer the question.
With the objects the same distance from the lamp, the tall block made the longer shadow.
Use the observation: the tall block made the longer shadow in this test.
The tall block made the longer shadow
The bead made the longer shadow
Predict: in winter, will daylight usually last longer or shorter than in summer?
The record supports the prediction that this winter day had fewer daylight hours than this summer day. Records help us compare observations.
Our daylight record shows 8 hours on a winter day and 16 hours on a summer day.
Read the record: 8 winter hours is fewer than 16 summer hours.
Which body part is linked with hearing?
We use our ears to hear sounds.
Ears are linked with hearing sounds.
A frog is an amphibian and a robin is a bird. They are both animals.
Look for two living animals, not a plant, rock, material or object.
Which action can change the shape of a soft piece of clay?
Squashing, bending, twisting or stretching can change the shape of some materials.
Some materials change shape when we squash, bend, twist or stretch them.
Which two objects could be grouped because they are made from metal?
A spoon and a key can both be made from metal. We group objects by a property or material.
Group objects using their material. A spoon and key can both be metal.
